title: Just and the Justifier
summary: Through history a vast store of wrath built up against our sin. Only Jesus could absorb it, stepping in as our propitiation.
exhortation: I want to zero in on one phrase: "This was to show God's righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins."

When I think about the story of Noah and the ark, the amazing thing isn't that Noah was saved, but that anyone was saved. What should have happened is that God wiped out all of humanity for the sin piling up higher and higher. What has been happening throughout history leading up to Jesus is a store of wrath: a massive store built by the sin of mankind over and over again.

The Law and the Prophets testified that we needed a righteousness apart from the law, because the law wasn't working. It wasn't correcting anything. It was magnifying the problem. But in his forbearance the Lord made a beautiful promise to Noah and put the rainbow in the sky. He would be patient. He would not destroy us as our sins deserve.

But what would happen to this immense store of wrath, growing bigger and bigger? God is just. He can't turn a blind eye to sin. Something had to be done. And so came the answer generations of prophets foretold. This vast store of wrath required an even greater store of mercy, righteousness and grace. What could withstand that tsunami of wrath we had earned? Only the Savior. Only Jesus.

When he asked the Father, "Is there another way? Can this cup just be poured out?" the answer was no. Jesus was the only way the wrath could be removed, and he stepped into our place. That is the wonderful word propitiation: Jesus, like a righteous shield, taking the wrath of God for us.
prayer: Jesus, thank you. It could only have been you. None of us could pay the price for sin except with eternal separation from you. And yet you came and absorbed the wrath of God, every drop. You drank the cup down to its dregs and took our sin, our shame and the wrath we deserved.
As we go about our day, fill our hearts with gratitude for what you've done, so that you would be glorified and your name lifted high in all the earth. We pray in Jesus' name.
